To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a mutation of the GDH gene causes hyperinsulinism and that this mutation results in unregulated GDH activity that enhances glutamine-stimulus insulin secretion.
a mutation in the GDH gene results in constitutive activation of GDH activity and that this unregulated elevation of GDH activity enhances insulin secretion, especially at low glucose concentrations.

a mutant glutamate dehyrogenase (GDH), with a mutation (Y 266 C) in the catalytic domain, has constitutively increased activity and that overexpression of this mutant GDH in MIN6 cells induces insulin secretion by glutamine at glucose concentrations of 2 and 5 mM but not 8--25 mM.

the molecular mechanism underlying the regulation of insulin release by glutamate dehydrogeanse.

the identification of a novel mutation in the GLUD1 gene in a patient with PHHI and the functional characterization of the mutant enzyme in COS-7 and MIN6-GDH cells, and the effect of the mutant enzyme overexpression on insulin secretion from MIN-6-GDH cells.
the role of GDH in glucose homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mutations of the GLUD1 gene, encoding GDH, are associated with PHHI, and that the mutant GDH induces insulin secretion at low glucose levels.
the Y266C mutation is the first GDH mutation to be identified in PHHI and that it results in constitutive activation of GDH activity, which in turn induces glutamine-stimulation of insulin secretion.
mutations of GLUD1 gene result in hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia of infancy and that the mutant enzyme is responsible for the hyperinsulinism.

the mutation of GDH results in the unregulated elevation of the enzyme activity, which leads to the enhanced oxidation of glutamate to alpha-ketoglutate and thereby stimulates insulin secretion, particularly at low glucose concentrations.
the mutation of the GLUD1 gene causes the unregulated increase of the activity of GDH, which results in the enhancement of glutamine-stimulating insulin secretion.
the unregulated elevation of GDH activity induces glutamine stimulated insulin secretion.

mutations in the GLUD1 gene, which encodes GDH, can result in hyperinsulism.
